newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh workers call strike over privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh workers call strike over privatisation.

text.p: Bangladesh's top labour union on Tuesday called for a 24-hour national strike on Wednesday to protest against the government's privatisation programme and to demand higher wages, union leaders said.

They said government-initiated talks failed on Tuesday night after the Sramik Karmachari Oikya Parishad (SKOP), the umbrella body of workers' federations, pressed for but did not receive firm commitments from authorities.
"We rejected a request to withdraw our strike... since we have not been assured that our demands would be considered," Kamrul Hassan, a senior SKOP leader told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We are determined to go ahead with our decision (to strike) to press for our demands."
S.A. Malek, political adviser to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, said he held talks with the SKOP leaders on Tuesday but failed to persuade them to call off the strike.
"We requested them to wait until the prime minister returns from abroad," he said. Hasina is on a private visit to the United States and is expected to retain early next month.
"The SKOP's demands centre on the government's major policy issues," he said, referring to Bangladesh's adoption of free market policies.
"We need to talk both within and outside parliament on some issues (including) the privatisation programme."
Hassan said the SKOP wanted the government to stop the privatisation of state-owned mills and retrenchment of workers.
"We are also demanding a separate wage commission for workers," he added.
He said at least 5,000 mills and factories had been closed since 1991 and thousands of workers at state-owned companies had been sacked.
In addition, the government recently called for bids for 13 public state companies being sold under its privatisation programme.
SKOP leaders expect nearly one million workers in both the public and private sectors will heed the call to strike.
